evidence:
ASK: instruction.md:1-17 asks for a full multi-user recruiting workspace on Node/Express/SQLite (instruction.md:13): per-job pipeline board with one-stage moves, shared manual ordering, Interview capacity, refusal with put-back and the colleague's name (instruction.md:3), all-or-none bulk moves and undo (:3), live updates within 15 s that preserve open card/draft/cursor (:5), paged long conversations, per-person unread and seen state, drafts surviving reload and sign-out scoped per user (:7), candidate portal with privacy rules (:9), Board/Conversations/Activity views (:11), persistence across restart with seed-once (:15). hireops_rules.md sections 1-7 define role permissions (401/403/404), optimistic versioning with 409 (sec. 3 'Two people at once'), bulk ordering, undo invalidation, activity log, live-update preservation (sec. 5), paging 30 at a time with stable scroll (sec. 6), candidate wording and data isolation (sec. 7). task.toml difficulty='hard' with matching difficulty_explanation. The smallest conforming submission is necessarily a server-backed multi-role app with auth, concurrency control, polling/SSE, and a messaging subsystem; a static page, single CRUD screen or mock cannot satisfy the brief. The golden is ~1.4k lines across src/index.js (426), board.js (373), threads.js (224), app.js (213), db.js (88), bootstrap.js (61). Template instruction.md is a placeholder ('CHANGE_ME'), so the ask is entirely task-authored.

GRADING DISCRIMINATES STUBS: gates/render/judge.toml:23 rejects 'A static picture or only a health response'; gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 requires UI-created job+candidate visible from an independent Observer context and rejects 'A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app'; constraints/prompt.md:9 forbids API-only writes and a same-context reload as independence. score.py:41-48 zeroes reward unless both gates pass and functional > floor 0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11, identical to template floor). Functional (43 criteria, weight 58.5) covers concurrency (hro_stale_refused 2.5), live board (2.5), bulk/undo (hro_bulk_* , hro_undo_* totalling 10), messaging/unread/seen/drafts (~17), candidate privacy (2.5), restart (1.5). Polish (5 binary, weight 12) needs live-update preservation, paging scroll anchoring, failed-send retention and session-resume drafts - all zero for a stub.

WEAK-APP PROBE (paper analysis, not executed): a login + jobs/candidates CRUD app with server persistence, email validation and no board rules, messaging, activity or live updates passes both gates and could earn hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1.0 = 2.0/58.5 = 0.034 (below the 0.05 floor -> reward 0). If the judge also credits hro_restart (1.5) despite absent notes/messages/activity, functional = 3.5/58.5 = 0.0598, which clears the floor; total reward would then be about 0.6*0.06 + 0.2*0 (polish) + 0.2*visual. Visual likert criteria (hro_vis_*) are judged across board, conversations and activity surfaces, so a CRUD-only app should rate low there; even an optimistic visual of 0.5 yields reward ~0.14 versus a golden expected near the top. This is bounded shaped partial credit for genuine (if small) server build work, not a stub earning the reward, and the floor is template-controlled (template tests/scoring.toml identical). A trivial tweak cannot earn the reward because no starter app exists: the agent must build /app from scratch.

CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE: brief leaves routes, names, layout, drag, transport (polling/SSE/sockets) and draft storage to the builder (hireops_rules.md:3-5, sec. 5, sec. 6 Drafts; instruction.md:11,13); criteria are phrased by observable behaviour ('whether tried through the UI or, if not offered, by replay; hiding it is optional'), so I found no way this row's demand for a real product forces one implementation. Fairness of individual criteria belongs to other rows.

RISK REASON: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The stub-versus-real separation above is therefore source analysis only; no weak-app or CRUD-only mutant has been scored by the configured judge, and the likert-to-[0,1] normalisation and judge behaviour on hro_restart for a feature-poor app are unmeasured. The verdict on the ask itself is Pass; the claim that a stub cannot earn meaningful reward remains Not exercised at runtime, so risk=true until a reward-discrimination run (e.g. CRUD-only mutant) is recorded.
